source_metadata.citation: Chang, Y.-W.; Sung, W.-C.; Chen, J.-Y. (Sung, W.-C. et al.) Effect of Hydroxymethylfurfural and Low-Molecular-Weight Chitosan on Formation of Acrylamide and Hydroxymethylfurfural in a Maillard Model System. Polymers 2021, 13 (12), 1901.
source_metadata.crossref_verified: 2026-08-27 via Europe PMC/OpenAlex record for 10.3390/polym13121901, Polymers 13(12):1901, 2021.
source_metadata.notes: MAILLARD-PATH HOLD-OUT (Wave U, 2026-08-27). Never use for calibration, refitting, or any promotion decision.

content_verification.quoted_method: 2.2. Preparation of Maillard Reaction Products (MRPs). MRPs were prepared by combining 0.5 g asparagine, 0.5 g chitosan, and 0.5 g glucose with 1% acetic acid following the method described by Chang et al. [16] with slight modifications. Solutions containing 0.5 g asparagine, 0.5 g glucose, and 0.5 g hydroxymethylfurfural in distilled water were also prepared. The pH value of each solution was first adjusted to 5.8 by adding 1 N sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and then 0.001 N NaOH to pH 6.0 and topped up with distilled water to 100 mL. Each solution was heated at 180 degC for 10, 20, and 30 min, followed by cooling in tap water.
content_verification.quoted_quantification: The acrylamide level from the Maillard reaction with internal standard was measured by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) following the method of Chang et al. [12]. The acrylamide calibration curve was built in the range of 0-3125 ppb using a UV detector at 210 nm. ... The HMF calibration curve was built in the range of 0.48-750 ppm at 40 degC using a UV detector.
content_verification.quantification_verdict: ADMISSIBLE WITH A STATED CAVEAT. Both analytes are read off authentic-standard calibration curves after SPE clean-up, so these are absolute concentrations of the reaction solution. 13C3-acrylamide is listed among the purchased chemicals and the method sentence says 'with internal standard', but the DETECTOR named is UV at 210 nm, not MS - so this cannot be called stable-isotope dilution, and co-eluting UV-absorbing Maillard products could bias the acrylamide value high. It cannot bias it by the factors this hold-out measures.

precursor_concentration_provenance.derivation: 0.5 g asparagine and 0.5 g glucose, each made up to 100 mL. Glucose MW 180.16 -> 0.5/180.16/0.1 L = 27.75 mM. The Chemicals section names 'L-asparagine monohydrate' (MW 150.13) -> 0.5/150.13/0.1 L = 33.30 mM; if the authors meant anhydrous asparagine (MW 132.12) it would be 37.85 mM. The monohydrate reading is used because it is the salt the paper says it bought. Glucose is limiting under either reading.
precursor_concentration_provenance.unstated_conditions: The vessel is not described. A 100 mL aqueous solution held at 180 degC is above the normal boiling point, so it must be sealed or aliquoted; the paper says neither. Water activity is therefore not measurable from the paper and is entered as 0.99 for a dilute aqueous solution. Recorded rather than hidden.

contamination_disclosure.what_is_contaminated: src/barrier_constants.FAST_BARRIERS['safety_risk_acrylamide'] = 30.83 kcal/mol is a declared transfer of the Knol et al. 2009/2010 lumped Asn+sugar->acrylamide Ea = 129 kJ/mol (10.1016/j.foodchem.2009.11.049), and that barrier sits on the network route producing this prediction. The TEMPERATURE dependence is Knol-anchored.
contamination_disclosure.what_is_not_contaminated: The absolute yield and, for the time-course pair, the TIME dependence. No acrylamide yield has ever been fitted in this repository. 10.3390/polym13121901 returns zero grep hits across data/, docs/, src/ and results/ (checked 2026-08-27).
contamination_disclosure.consequence: The 10 min / 30 min pair from this paper is scored as a test of the model's TIME dependence at fixed temperature, which the Knol Ea transfer cannot help with.

vehicle_note: 1% acetic acid, back-titrated to pH 6.0 (Figure 3B arm). The model has no acetate species; the only thing this vehicle can express in the payload is the pH, which is 6.0 in BOTH arms. The two arms therefore receive IDENTICAL model inputs while the paper measures 1459 vs 832 ppb at 30 min - a 1.75x difference the model cannot resolve by construction. See the cross-bundle ordinal record in results/validation/maillard_path_holdout_frozen_predictions.md.

buffer.provenance_note: Chang / Sung et al. 2021, Polymers 13(12):1901, sec. 2.2, verbatim as carried in this bundle's content_verification.quoted_method: 'MRPs were prepared by combining 0.5 g asparagine, 0.5 g chitosan, and 0.5 g glucose with 1% acetic acid' and 'The pH value of each solution was first adjusted to 5.8 by adding 1 N sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and then 0.001 N NaOH to pH 6.0 and topped up with distilled water to 100 mL.' Acetic acid back-titrated with NaOH to pH 6.0 IS an acetate buffer, which is why this is recorded as a buffer and not as water. SOURCE PAPER NOT ON DISK; second-hand. TWO AMBIGUITIES, REPORTED NOT RESOLVED: (i) '1%' carries no w/v-vs-v/v basis, so the total acetate is 0.167-0.175 M and 0.17 is the midpoint; (ii) the quoted sentence ties the 1% acetic acid to a formulation that ALSO contains 0.5 g chitosan, while this bundle's vehicle_note labels the same arm merely '1% acetic acid, back-titrated to pH 6.0 (Figure 3B arm)'. Whether the scored arm contains chitosan cannot be settled from the quoted text.

metadata.notes: family is deliberately NOT 'safety', so Recommender.predict_from_steps produces the number instead of the lumped predict_acrylamide solver. This is the 30 min end of a fixed-temperature TIME COURSE; its partner bundle is mp_holdout_glucose_asparagine_180C_10min_Chang2021.

Acrylamide.target_quote: 3.3. Effect of Chitosan on Formation of Acrylamide and HMF. Concentration of acrylamide in the solutions containing 0.5% glucose and 0.5% asparagine after 10, 20, and 30 min of heating was 28, 912, and 1459 ppb, respectively (Figure 3B).
Acrylamide.molar_basis: ppb of the reaction solution (ug/L), read off an acrylamide calibration curve built over 0-3125 ppb. Figure 3B is the 1% acetic acid arm; Figure 3A is the deionized-water arm. The two arms are kept in SEPARATE bundles because mixing them is exactly the kind of silent arm-swap this campaign exists to stop.
Acrylamide.note: The 30 min end of the time-course pair. Measured 28 -> 1459 ppb over 10 -> 30 min is a 52.1x rise at constant temperature.
